A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse VideoGen2 work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support a complete comparison; v4 adds references and a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation benchmarks, kernel measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A–E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including quality, efficiency, warmup-free, and clustering-ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains independent query/key clustering, semantic-aware permutation, centroid-based top-p selection, centroid caching, and the dynamic-block sparse attention kernel. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Penguin prompts for text-to-video and VBench prompt-image pairs for image-to-video, retaining the same Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain dense attention, SVG and its FP8 configuration, SpargeAttention, XAttention, and the FlashInfer kernel comparator. Newly cited systems are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: The model configurations, 720p resolution, metrics, cluster settings, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Both retain 30% warmup in Table 1 and the separate zero-warmup evaluation in Appendix B.

E4.justification: The centroid-cache, quality-efficiency, permutation, cluster-count, and shared-clustering analyses are retained. Appendix E also preserves the same backend-sensitivity observations and cross-model comparisons.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses testing with multiple random seeds and explains omitting error bars by asserting highly deterministic results. v2 contains no equivalent seed disclosure. No seed count, quantitative uncertainty estimate, or explicit increase in runs is provided.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–12 retain their numerical results, rankings, plots, and video examples. The limited addition is Checklist item 7's unquantified qualitative finding that results are highly deterministic and reproducible across random seeds.

T1.justification: The permutation-equivalence derivation in Section 4.1 and the centroid-score formulas in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. The checklist references the existing proof without adding mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both retain the same training-free sparse-attention contribution, claimed Pareto quality-efficiency trade-off, and headline speedups of up to 2.30× on HunyuanVideo and 1.89× on Wan2.1.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the limitation concerning generalization beyond DiTs. Appendix E preserves the explanations involving numerical sensitivity, context length, and attention's runtime share. The checklist adds only generic societal-impact qualifications.

D1.justification: v4 adds a direct SVG2 repository link and an open-source statement to the front matter and abstract; v2 lacks this access information. Technical settings remain unchanged. Checklist item 5 still promises release upon publication, leaving inconsistent release-status wording.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds seven references covering SANA, DC-AE/DC-Gen, and LongLive, with brief descriptions of their acceleration approaches. Earlier references are retained, and SVG2's central positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The scientific narrative remains largely verbatim. v4 adds the checklist and short related-work/code passages, edits author, affiliation, and venue text, and removes Appendix E.2's sentence promising a future Table 1 revision.

P2.justification: All twelve figures and six tables retain their scientific display content and designs. The repository header, text and figure reflow, expanded references, and checklist insertion alter layout and shift the appendices without substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The explicit repository pointer and relevant additions to Section 2 modestly improve usability and research context. Methods and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. The vague seed-stability assertion and inconsistent code-release wording limit the documentation gains.
